project.name: AgenticAI_Chatbot_Using_RAG
project.description: A production-ready AI chatbot with retrieval-augmented generation, conversation memory, PDF processing, and smart answer routing. A FastAPI backend routes each request through a LangGraph agent that chooses document RAG, a plain LLM reply, or web search, using FAISS and Cohere for retrieval.

nodes.name: agent.py
nodes.summary: Implements the LangGraph chat agent that routes each query to RAG or a direct LLM/search path, keeps in-memory session history, and indexes PDF text in per-user FAISS stores.
nodes.languageNotes: LangGraph StateGraph with a conditional router: document-similar queries pass through a RAG prompt node before the LLM, and non-RAG queries may use a Tavily ReAct agent.

nodes.name: AgentState
nodes.summary: LangGraph state schema carrying the message list, user and session ids, the RAG decision, similarity threshold, and retrieved documents.
nodes.languageNotes: TypedDict whose messages channel uses LangGraph's add_messages reducer.

nodes.name: MemoryManager
nodes.summary: In-memory store of per-session chat turns that timestamps each appended message and can return or clear a session's history.

nodes.name: RAGManager
nodes.summary: Manages per-user in-memory FAISS indexes with Cohere embeddings, including PDF chunking, similarity scoring, reranked retrieval, and document listing.

nodes.name: router_node
nodes.summary: Compares the latest user query with the user's indexed documents and, when similarity exceeds the threshold, loads reranked excerpts and selects the RAG path.

nodes.name: rag_node
nodes.summary: Rewrites the latest user message into a citation-constrained prompt that includes numbered excerpts, source names, page numbers, and relevance scores.

nodes.name: _build_agent_node
nodes.summary: Returns a graph node bound to a chat model that answers from retrieved context, or uses a Tavily ReAct agent when search is enabled.

nodes.name: _build_graph
nodes.summary: Compiles a LangGraph that starts at the router, branches to the RAG node or the agent, and always finishes after the agent node.

nodes.name: get_response
nodes.summary: Builds a Groq or OpenAI chat model, optionally attaches Tavily search, replays session history, and runs the compiled graph to return the assistant text.

nodes.name: process_pdf
nodes.summary: Extracts page text from a PDF path and indexes the resulting chunks in the user's FAISS store.

nodes.name: _extract_pdf_pages
nodes.summary: Reads a PDF with pdfplumber and falls back to PyPDF2, returning page-number and text pairs for pages that contain enough text.

nodes.name: get_chat_history
nodes.summary: Returns the in-memory message list stored for a chat session.

nodes.name: clear_chat_history
nodes.summary: Drops the in-memory message history for a chat session.

nodes.name: get_user_documents
nodes.summary: Returns the unique source filenames currently indexed for a user.

nodes.name: client.py
nodes.summary: Python HTTP client for the FastAPI backend, covering health checks, model listing, chat sessions, document upload, retrieval, and web search.

nodes.name: BackendClient
nodes.summary: Requests wrapper that calls backend routes for health, models, sessions, messages, file and URL uploads, retrieval, search, and document listing.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Central runtime configuration that loads environment variables and defines paths, API keys, model catalogs, RAG chunking and retrieval settings, and agent modes.

nodes.name: embeddings.py
nodes.summary: Provides a shared embeddings adapter that prefers Cohere and falls back to Google Gemini embeddings when Cohere is unavailable or fails.
nodes.languageNotes: Subclasses LangChain Embeddings and tries Cohere embed-english-v3.0 before Google text-embedding-004 for both documents and queries.

nodes.name: HybridEmbeddings
nodes.summary: LangChain embeddings implementation that embeds documents and queries with Cohere first and Google Gemini embeddings second.

nodes.name: retriever.py
nodes.summary: Chunks uploaded document pages into FAISS records and retrieves them with an initial vector search followed by Cohere reranking.

nodes.name: process_and_index
nodes.summary: Splits page text into overlapping chunks tagged with source, page, and user metadata, then upserts them into the user's FAISS index.

nodes.name: retrieve_documents
nodes.summary: Loads a user's FAISS index, recalls an initial candidate set, and reranks those passages with Cohere or falls back to distance-based scores.

nodes.name: vector_store.py
nodes.summary: Persists one FAISS index per user on disk and exposes load, document upsert, and unique source-filename listing.

nodes.name: VectorStoreManager
nodes.summary: Loads and saves a FAISS index per user id, adding documents to an existing index or creating one, and lists the unique source filenames stored in it.

nodes.name: database.py
nodes.summary: SQLAlchemy engine, session factory, and declarative Base for the chatbot backend. Provides the FastAPI session dependency and creates tables at startup, enabling SQLite multi-thread access when DATABASE_URL is a SQLite path.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses SQLAlchemy 2.0 DeclarativeBase. get_db is a generator dependency that closes the session in a finally block, and SQLite engines pass check_same_thread=False.

nodes.name: Base
nodes.summary: Declarative base class that every ORM model inherits so table metadata is registered for create_all.

nodes.name: get_db
nodes.summary: FastAPI dependency that opens a SQLAlchemy session, yields it to the request, and closes it when the request finishes.

nodes.name: init_db
nodes.summary: Imports the ORM models so they register on Base.metadata, then creates any missing tables. Called once from the application lifespan.

nodes.name: main.py
nodes.summary: FastAPI application that exposes session, message, document, RAG retrieval, and web-search routes and serves the static single-page app. A lifespan hook creates database tables on startup, and CORS is configured from backend settings.
nodes.languageNotes: The lifespan async context manager calls init_db before traffic is served. Route handlers take a request-scoped session through Depends(get_db), and StaticFiles mounts expose /css, /js, and /assets.

nodes.name: lifespan
nodes.summary: Application lifespan hook that creates SQLite tables via init_db before the API starts accepting requests.

nodes.name: ping
nodes.summary: Keepalive handler for GET /ping that returns a small JSON pong for uptime monitors.

nodes.name: health_check
nodes.summary: GET /health handler that reports database connectivity plus whether Cohere and Tavily API keys are configured.

nodes.name: get_models
nodes.summary: GET /models handler that returns the configured LLM catalog grouped by provider.

nodes.name: list_sessions
nodes.summary: GET /sessions handler that lists a user's chat sessions ordered by most recently updated.

nodes.name: create_session
nodes.summary: POST /sessions handler that inserts a new ChatSession from the request body and returns the persisted row.

nodes.name: get_session
nodes.summary: GET /sessions/{session_id} handler that loads one session and its message history, or raises 404 when the id is missing.

nodes.name: update_session
nodes.summary: PATCH /sessions/{session_id} handler that updates title, model, or mode on an existing session.

nodes.name: delete_session
nodes.summary: DELETE /sessions/{session_id} handler that removes a session and, through the ORM cascade, its messages.

nodes.name: save_message
nodes.summary: POST /sessions/{session_id}/messages handler that appends a user or assistant message and sets a short title from the first user message.

nodes.name: upload_document
nodes.summary: POST /upload handler that parses an uploaded file or URL, indexes the pages into FAISS, and records the document in SQLite.

nodes.name: list_documents
nodes.summary: GET /documents handler that lists a user's indexed documents, newest first.

nodes.name: retrieve_endpoint
nodes.summary: POST /retrieve handler that queries the FAISS index and returns chunks whose relevance meets the request threshold.

nodes.name: search_endpoint
nodes.summary: POST /search handler that forwards the query to the Tavily search service and returns structured results.

nodes.name: serve_spa
nodes.summary: GET / handler that returns the frontend index.html when it is present on disk.

nodes.name: GET /ping
nodes.summary: Keepalive route handled by ping for free-tier uptime monitors.

nodes.name: GET /health
nodes.summary: Health route handled by health_check. Returns HealthResponse with database, Cohere, and Tavily status.

nodes.name: GET /models
nodes.summary: Model catalog route handled by get_models. Returns the configured LLM list grouped by provider.

nodes.name: GET /sessions
nodes.summary: Session list route handled by list_sessions. Returns SessionSummary rows for a user_id query parameter.

nodes.name: POST /sessions
nodes.summary: Session creation route handled by create_session. Accepts SessionCreate and returns the new SessionSchema with HTTP 201.

nodes.name: GET /sessions/{session_id}
nodes.summary: Session detail route handled by get_session. Returns one session plus its full message history.

nodes.name: PATCH /sessions/{session_id}
nodes.summary: Session update route handled by update_session. Accepts SessionUpdate for title, model, and mode.

nodes.name: DELETE /sessions/{session_id}
nodes.summary: Session deletion route handled by delete_session. Responds with HTTP 204 after removing the session and its messages.

nodes.name: POST /sessions/{session_id}/messages
nodes.summary: Message append route handled by save_message. Accepts MessageCreate and returns the stored MessageSchema with HTTP 201.

nodes.name: POST /upload
nodes.summary: Document ingestion route handled by upload_document. Accepts a file upload or a URL and returns UploadResponse after indexing.

nodes.name: GET /documents
nodes.summary: Indexed-document list route handled by list_documents. Returns DocumentSchema rows for a user.

nodes.name: POST /retrieve
nodes.summary: Hybrid RAG route handled by retrieve_endpoint. Accepts RetrieveRequest and returns RetrieveResponse chunks from FAISS plus Cohere reranking.

nodes.name: POST /search
nodes.summary: Web search route handled by search_endpoint. Accepts SearchRequest and returns a Tavily SearchResponse.

nodes.name: GET /
nodes.summary: SPA entry route handled by serve_spa. Returns the frontend index.html file.

nodes.name: api.py
nodes.summary: Pydantic request and response schemas for sessions, messages, document upload, RAG retrieval, web search, and health checks.
nodes.languageNotes: Pydantic v2 models. Session, message, and document schemas that mirror ORM rows set model_config from_attributes so FastAPI can serialize SQLAlchemy instances.

nodes.name: SessionCreate
nodes.summary: Request body for creating a chat session, with user id, title, model, and mode defaults for a general session.

nodes.name: SessionUpdate
nodes.summary: Partial update body for a session. Title, model, and mode are each optional.

nodes.name: CitationSchema
nodes.summary: Citation attached to a message, carrying an id, source name, page or row locator, and snippet.

nodes.name: MessageSchema
nodes.summary: API representation of a stored chat message, including role, content, optional citations, and created_at. Reads directly from ORM rows.

nodes.name: SessionSchema
nodes.summary: Full session response with metadata and the nested message history.

nodes.name: SessionSummary
nodes.summary: Compact session list item with metadata and timestamps, used by the sessions list route.

nodes.name: MessageCreate
nodes.summary: Request body for appending a user or assistant message, with an optional list of citations.

nodes.name: UploadResponse
nodes.summary: Response after document ingestion, reporting document id, filename, file type, chunk count, and user id.

nodes.name: RetrieveRequest
nodes.summary: RAG query body with the user id, a relevance threshold defaulting to 0.40, and a top_k bounded from 1 to 20.

nodes.name: RetrievedChunk
nodes.summary: One retrieved excerpt with source, page, snippet, and a relevance score.

nodes.name: RetrieveResponse
nodes.summary: RAG retrieval result containing the matching chunks, a used_rag flag, and the original query.

nodes.name: SearchRequest
nodes.summary: Web search request with a query and max_results bounded from 1 to 10.

nodes.name: SearchResult
nodes.summary: One Tavily hit with title, URL, snippet, and score.

nodes.name: SearchResponse
nodes.summary: Web search response holding the result list and the query string that produced it.

nodes.name: DocumentSchema
nodes.summary: API view of an indexed document: id, filename, file type, chunk count, and indexed_at. Reads from the ORM row.

nodes.name: HealthResponse
nodes.summary: Health payload with an overall status and a map of service names to connection or configuration state.

nodes.name: db.py
nodes.summary: SQLAlchemy ORM models for chat sessions, messages, and indexed documents, stored in the sessions, messages, and documents tables.
nodes.languageNotes: ChatSession.messages uses cascade all, delete-orphan and orders messages by created_at, so deleting a session removes its messages.

nodes.name: _uuid
nodes.summary: Returns a new UUID4 string used as the default primary key for sessions, messages, and documents.

nodes.name: ChatSession
nodes.summary: ORM model for a chat session, storing user id, title, model, mode, and timestamps, with a cascade relationship to its messages.

nodes.name: Message
nodes.summary: ORM model for a chat message, storing role, content, JSON citations, and a cascading foreign key to sessions.

nodes.name: Document
nodes.summary: ORM model for an indexed file or URL, recording filename, file type, chunk count, and indexed_at for a user.

nodes.name: parser.py
nodes.summary: Multi-format document parser that turns PDF, DOCX, CSV, Excel, plain text, and web URLs into page dictionaries for indexing.
nodes.languageNotes: Every parser returns a list of dicts with page_number, text, and metadata so the indexer can treat files and URLs the same way.

nodes.name: parse_file
nodes.summary: Dispatches a local file to the PDF, DOCX, CSV, Excel, or text parser based on the filename extension.

nodes.name: parse_url
nodes.summary: Public entry point that extracts article text from a web URL into page dictionaries.

nodes.name: _parse_pdf
nodes.summary: Extracts per-page PDF text and tables with pdfplumber, falling back to PyPDF2 when that extraction fails.

nodes.name: _parse_docx
nodes.summary: Reads a Word document, splitting paragraphs on headings and appending table rows as text sections.

nodes.name: _parse_csv
nodes.summary: Reads a CSV file and packs header-plus-row groups into page-sized text chunks.

nodes.name: _parse_excel
nodes.summary: Loads each Excel sheet with pandas and emits row-range chunks as page dictionaries.

nodes.name: _parse_text
nodes.summary: Reads plain text or Markdown and groups paragraphs into size-bounded pages.

nodes.name: _parse_url
nodes.summary: Fetches a URL with trafilatura and, if that yields no text, scrapes it with requests and BeautifulSoup, then splits the article into chunks.

nodes.name: _split_into_chunks
nodes.summary: Packs paragraphs into chunks that stay within a character budget, used by the URL parser.

nodes.name: search.py
nodes.summary: Tavily web search service that runs a single query, merges several queries with URL deduplication, and expands a question into a few focused sub-queries.
nodes.languageNotes: The Tavily client is imported inside search, so a missing package surfaces only when a query actually runs. Empty results are returned when TAVILY_API_KEY is unset.

nodes.name: search
nodes.summary: Runs one Tavily search and maps hits into SearchResult items inside a SearchResponse.

nodes.name: multi_search
nodes.summary: Runs up to four sub-queries, drops duplicate URLs, and returns the combined hits sorted by score.

nodes.name: generate_sub_queries
nodes.summary: Expands a research question into up to three search strings, adding a recency variant and an examples variant when the wording calls for them.

nodes.name: .env.example
nodes.summary: Environment template listing Groq, Tavily, Cohere, and optional LLM API keys plus server host, CORS origins, and the SQLite database URL loaded at startup.
nodes.languageNotes: Placeholder values only; python-dotenv reads a copied .env so secrets stay out of version control.

nodes.name: Procfile
nodes.summary: Render and Railway process declaration that starts the FastAPI app with uvicorn, binding to the platform-assigned port.
nodes.languageNotes: A single web process type runs uvicorn backend.main:app and uses $PORT instead of a fixed local port.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Getting-started guide for the RAG chatbot covering project layout, local setup, environment variables, FastAPI endpoints, and the LangGraph router-to-agent workflow.

nodes.name: requirements.txt
nodes.summary: Python package list for the FastAPI server, LangChain and LangGraph providers, FAISS retrieval, PDF and document parsing, and SQLAlchemy persistence.
nodes.languageNotes: Packages are unpinned, so installs follow the latest compatible releases of FastAPI, LangChain, and FAISS.

nodes.name: animations.css
nodes.summary: Motion stylesheet for the static chatbot SPA: keyframe animations and utility classes for fades, slides, skeletons, the streaming cursor, spinners, and progress fills. Honors prefers-reduced-motion and is linked from frontend/index.html, reusing color and radius tokens from main.css.
nodes.languageNotes: A prefers-reduced-motion media query collapses animation and transition durations to near zero for the whole document.

nodes.name: components.css
nodes.summary: Component stylesheet for the chatbot UI, covering buttons, inputs, session items, messages, thought steps, citations, code blocks, the input dock, modals, the welcome screen, and upload controls. Loaded by frontend/index.html and styled with design tokens from main.css plus motion classes from animations.css.
nodes.languageNotes: BEM-style class names consume custom properties (colors, radii, transitions) declared in main.css rather than hard-coding the theme.

nodes.name: main.css
nodes.summary: Foundation stylesheet that defines the dark-by-default design tokens, light-theme overrides, app-shell layout (sidebar, top bar, chat area, input dock), typography, and the mobile breakpoint. Linked first from frontend/index.html so animations.css and components.css can reuse its custom properties.
nodes.languageNotes: Custom properties live on :root with a [data-theme="light"] override, and an @import loads Inter and JetBrains Mono.

nodes.name: devcontainer.json
nodes.summary: Dev Container spec for a Python 3.11 image that installs project requirements and Streamlit, forwards FastAPI on port 8000 and Streamlit on 8501, and starts the Streamlit UI with frontend/app.py when the container attaches.
nodes.languageNotes: JSON with comments (JSONC). postAttachCommand launches Streamlit; forwardPorts exposes the FastAPI and Streamlit ports.

nodes.name: config.json
nodes.summary: Understand Anything output-language configuration. It sets outputLanguage to en so generated graph text is written in English.

nodes.name: Pipfile
nodes.summary: Pipenv dependency manifest that pins Python 3.13 and leaves both the packages and dev-packages sections empty, so it does not currently declare installable project dependencies.
nodes.languageNotes: Pipenv TOML-like syntax. The PyPI source is the only populated section.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker that makes backend importable as a Python package. It does not re-export the FastAPI app or other submodules.

nodes.name: models.py
nodes.summary: Legacy Pydantic models for an earlier chat API: chat requests and responses, history and clear-history payloads, a user-documents request, and a health payload. It is a sibling of the backend.models package and is not re-exported by backend/models/__init__.py.
nodes.languageNotes: Public Pydantic BaseModel classes. HealthResponse is also defined, with a different shape, in backend/models/api.py.

nodes.name: ChatRequest
nodes.summary: Request body for a chat turn: model name and provider, system prompt, messages, search flag, optional user and session ids, and a similarity threshold between 0 and 1.

nodes.name: ChatResponse
nodes.summary: Chat reply payload containing the assistant response text plus the session id and user id.

nodes.name: ChatHistoryRequest
nodes.summary: Request body that identifies a session whose chat history should be loaded.

nodes.name: ClearHistoryRequest
nodes.summary: Request body that identifies a session whose stored chat history should be cleared.

nodes.name: UserDocumentsRequest
nodes.summary: Request body that identifies a user whose indexed documents should be listed.

nodes.name: HealthResponse
nodes.summary: Legacy health payload with a status string and a message. A separate HealthResponse class lives in backend/models/api.py.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker for backend.models. It does not re-export api.py, db.py, or the legacy backend/models.py module.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker for the backend RAG package. Retrieval and embedding modules live beside it and are not re-exported here.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker for backend services such as document parsing, the vector store, and web search. It does not re-export those modules.

nodes.name: .gitkeep
nodes.summary: Empty placeholder that keeps the data directory under version control when no runtime documents or indexes are committed.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker for the frontend directory. The Streamlit entry point is frontend/app.py, which this file does not import.

nodes.name: app.py
nodes.summary: Streamlit UI for the RAG chatbot. It keeps session state, renders chat and document controls, and calls the FastAPI backend over HTTP at BACKEND_URL (default http://localhost:8000) for chat, history, PDF upload, and document listing.
nodes.languageNotes: Most of the page is module-level Streamlit script. Backend access goes through requests, and the connection error tells the operator to run uvicorn backend.main:app. It does not import backend.config.

nodes.name: _init_state
nodes.summary: Seeds Streamlit session state with a new session id, the default user, and empty chat, document, and response fields when those keys are missing.

nodes.name: _api
nodes.summary: Sends an HTTP request to the FastAPI backend and surfaces Streamlit errors when the server is unreachable or the call fails. Callers use it for /chat, /chat-history, /clear-history, /upload-pdf, and /user-documents.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: Static shell for the AI Assistant Pro single-page app. It lays out the chat, sidebar, upload, and citation UI, links the three local stylesheets, and loads the browser scripts ending with frontend/js/app.js.

nodes.name: api.js
nodes.summary: Browser REST client exposed as window.API. It calls the FastAPI backend for sessions, messages, document upload and listing, RAG retrieve, web search, and health, using window.CONFIG.BACKEND_URL when set.
nodes.languageNotes: IIFE assigned to window.API. Nested functions were not emitted by the structure extractor; significant ones are recorded from source.

nodes.name: request
nodes.summary: Shared fetch wrapper that prefixes the backend base URL, sends JSON or FormData, and throws with the API error detail when the response is not ok.

nodes.name: retrieve
nodes.summary: POSTs a query, user id, top-k, and similarity threshold to the backend /retrieve endpoint and returns matching document chunks.

nodes.name: app.js
nodes.summary: SPA orchestrator that wires the chat UI, keeps session and mode state, and runs the send pipeline: persist the user message, retrieve RAG chunks, optionally search the web, then stream a Puter.js completion.
nodes.languageNotes: Private IIFE. It talks to sibling modules through the window.API, window.Chat, window.UI, and window.PuterClient globals rather than ES module imports.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Bootstraps theme, model, and mode from local storage, binds DOM events, and loads the user's sessions and documents in parallel.

nodes.name: _bindEvents
nodes.summary: Attaches listeners for send, mode and model changes, new chat, theme, sidebar, file and URL upload, search toggle, citation modal, session search, and starter prompts.

nodes.name: _onSend
nodes.summary: Runs one chat turn: ensures a session, renders and saves the user message, retrieves document chunks and optional web results, streams the model reply, then saves the assistant message.

nodes.name: _selectSession
nodes.summary: Loads a saved session from the backend, restores its messages, mode, and model, and refreshes the session list highlight.

nodes.name: _deleteSession
nodes.summary: Deletes a chat session after confirmation, clears the transcript when it was active, and reloads the session list.

nodes.name: _handleFileUpload
nodes.summary: Validates a dropped or chosen document, uploads it through the backend, and refreshes the indexed document list.

nodes.name: _onUrlSubmit
nodes.summary: Validates a web URL from the ingest modal, asks the backend to index it, and refreshes the document list.

nodes.name: chat.js
nodes.summary: Chat transcript renderer exposed as window.Chat. It builds user and assistant bubbles, streams tokens with thought steps and citation cards, and restores prior session history.

nodes.name: appendUserMessage
nodes.summary: Appends a user message bubble with an avatar initial and timestamp, then scrolls the chat area to the bottom.

nodes.name: startAssistantMessage
nodes.summary: Inserts an assistant bubble and returns controllers to add thought steps, stream markdown tokens, finalize citations, and show errors.

nodes.name: showThinking
nodes.summary: Shows a temporary skeleton placeholder in the chat area while a reply is being prepared.

nodes.name: renderHistory
nodes.summary: Clears the chat area and redraws a saved session, rendering user text and assistant markdown with citation cards and syntax highlighting.

nodes.name: config.example.js
nodes.summary: Sample window.CONFIG for the static SPA. BACKEND_URL is the Python API origin consumed by api.js; PUTER_TOKEN is a placeholder for Puter.js model access. The page loads /js/config.js, not this example.

nodes.name: puter_client.js
nodes.summary: window.PuterClient wrapper around puter.ai.chat. It streams or returns a full completion and builds mode-specific system prompts that inject RAG excerpts and web search results.

nodes.name: streamChat
nodes.summary: Streams a Puter.js chat completion, forwarding each text token to onToken and reporting completion or failure through callbacks.

nodes.name: chat
nodes.summary: Requests a non-streaming Puter.js completion and returns the full response text.

nodes.name: buildSystemPrompt
nodes.summary: Builds the system prompt for general, document, research, or code mode and appends numbered RAG chunks and web search snippets for citation.

nodes.name: ui.js
nodes.summary: window.UI helpers for theme, sidebar, session and document lists, toasts, citation and URL modals, and the file drop overlay used by the static chat page.

nodes.name: setTheme
nodes.summary: Applies the light or dark theme on the document element, stores it, and swaps the highlight.js stylesheet to match.

nodes.name: renderSessionList
nodes.summary: Renders chat sessions grouped by date and wires click handlers so the app can open or delete a session.

nodes.name: renderDocList
nodes.summary: Renders the sidebar list of indexed documents with a type icon and a shortened filename.

nodes.name: showUploadToast
nodes.summary: Shows the upload progress toast and restarts its progress-bar animation for the file or URL being indexed.

nodes.name: showToast
nodes.summary: Shows a short-lived info, success, or error toast and removes it after a few seconds.

nodes.name: showCitationModal
nodes.summary: Opens the citation modal and fills it with the source label, optional page, and snippet for a retrieved chunk.

nodes.name: initDropzone
nodes.summary: Listens for document drag-and-drop, toggles the drop overlay, and passes the first dropped file to the upload handler.

nodes.name: utils.js
nodes.summary: window.Utils helpers for markdown rendering with citation badges, syntax highlighting and copy buttons, HTML escaping, timestamps, date groups, and ids.

nodes.name: renderMarkdown
nodes.summary: Parses markdown with marked and turns bracketed numbers such as [1] into clickable citation badges.

nodes.name: highlightCode
nodes.summary: Highlights code blocks with highlight.js and wraps each one with a language label and a copy button.

nodes.name: copyText
nodes.summary: Copies text to the clipboard with the async Clipboard API, falling back to a temporary textarea and execCommand.

nodes.name: formatDateGroup
nodes.summary: Buckets an ISO timestamp into Today, Yesterday, Previous 7 Days, Previous 30 Days, or Earlier for the session list.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with README.md, the getting-started guide for this RAG chatbot. It covers the project layout, local setup, environment variables, the FastAPI endpoints, and the LangGraph path from router to agent. requirements.txt names the libraries behind that design: the FastAPI server, LangChain and LangGraph providers, FAISS retrieval, document parsing, and SQLAlchemy persistence. Together they tell you what the app does before you open a single module.

tour.title: Runtime Configuration
tour.description: The setup in the README lands in backend/config.py, the settings module imported by the API, database, retrieval, and search code. It loads environment variables and defines paths, API keys, model catalogs, RAG chunking and retrieval settings, and agent modes. .env.example is the template for that load: Groq, Tavily, Cohere, and optional LLM keys, plus the server host, CORS origins, and the SQLite database URL. Later steps read these values instead of choosing models or chunk sizes on their own.
tour.languageLesson: A settings module that reads environment variables once keeps secrets out of source control. The example env file documents every key the process expects, and the rest of the app imports the resulting constants.

tour.title: API Schemas
tour.description: Before the routes, the API schemas layer names every payload the server accepts and returns. backend/models/api.py defines Pydantic models for sessions, messages, document upload, RAG retrieval, web search, and health checks. backend/models.py is the earlier chat contract — chat requests and responses, history and clear-history payloads, a user-documents request, and a health payload — and lives beside the models package as its own module. The session-based schemas are the ones the FastAPI routes in the next steps use.
tour.languageLesson: Pydantic models are classes with typed fields. FastAPI uses them to validate JSON, document the API, and serialize responses, so this file is the contract between the browser and the server.

tour.title: Conversation Storage
tour.description: The data layer is what those session and message schemas are stored as. backend/database.py builds the SQLAlchemy engine and session factory, provides the FastAPI session dependency, and creates tables at startup, enabling SQLite multi-thread access when DATABASE_URL is a SQLite path from the settings module. backend/models/db.py maps chat sessions, messages, and indexed documents onto the sessions, messages, and documents tables. Route handlers in the next step borrow a session from this dependency whenever they list, insert, or delete a conversation.
tour.languageLesson: SQLAlchemy's declarative base turns a Python class into a table. A dependency function yields a session for one request and closes it afterward, so handlers share an engine without sharing a connection.

tour.title: FastAPI Application
tour.description: backend/main.py is the process entry point. The dependency walk starts here: the module imports config, the database, both model modules, the retriever, the parser, and web search, then builds the FastAPI app. A lifespan hook creates the database tables on startup, and CORS is taken from the settings module. GET /health returns database, Cohere, and Tavily status; GET /models returns the configured LLM list grouped by provider; GET / serves the static single-page app.
tour.languageLesson: A FastAPI lifespan context manager runs setup before the server accepts traffic and cleanup on shutdown. Each route function can declare a Pydantic response model so health and model payloads stay aligned with the schema module.

tour.title: Session and Answer Routes
tour.description: These five routes are the conversation loop the clients call. POST /sessions accepts SessionCreate and returns the new session; POST /sessions/{session_id}/messages accepts MessageCreate and stores the turn through the database dependency. POST /upload accepts a file or a URL and returns UploadResponse after indexing; POST /retrieve returns reranked FAISS chunks; POST /search returns a Tavily SearchResponse. Saving the message, fetching document evidence, and fetching web evidence are separate calls, which is how the browser assembles one grounded reply.

tour.title: Document Parsing
tour.description: POST /upload reaches backend/services/parser.py before anything is embedded. The parser turns PDF, DOCX, CSV, Excel, plain text, and web URLs into page dictionaries for indexing. One page shape lets the same upload route feed every format into the retrieval pipeline. This is the step between a file the user drops on the page and the chunks the vector index stores.

tour.title: Retrieval Pipeline
tour.description: From main.py the import walk reaches the retriever, then the embedding adapter and the on-disk index. backend/rag/retriever.py chunks the parser's page dictionaries into FAISS records and retrieves them with a vector search followed by Cohere reranking, which is what POST /retrieve returns. backend/rag/embeddings.py prefers Cohere and falls back to Google Gemini embeddings when Cohere is unavailable. backend/services/vector_store.py persists one FAISS index per user, and data/.gitkeep keeps that data directory in version control when the runtime indexes are not committed.
tour.languageLesson: An adapter class hides which embedding provider is active. Callers ask for vectors; the adapter tries the preferred provider and substitutes the fallback, so chunking and search stay the same when a key is missing.

tour.title: Web Search
tour.description: Document RAG is one evidence path; live web search is the other. backend/services/search.py runs a Tavily query, merges several queries while deduplicating URLs, and can expand one question into a few focused sub-queries. It builds SearchResult and SearchResponse from the API schemas, the same types POST /search returns. The chat UI calls this when the selected mode needs sources outside the uploaded documents.

tour.title: LangGraph Router
tour.description: The README describes a LangGraph router-to-agent workflow, and backend/agent.py is where that workflow lives. The module routes each query to document RAG or a direct LLM/search path, keeps in-memory session history, and indexes PDF text in per-user FAISS stores, importing the shared config from the settings step. The HTTP routes reached from main.py call the parser, retriever, and search services on their own. Read the agent for the routing design the project documents; the SPA in the next step makes a similar choice by calling retrieve and search before it streams a completion.
tour.languageLesson: LangGraph models one turn as a state graph. Node functions read and update a shared state object, and conditional edges pick the next node — a document path or a direct model/search path — until the graph finishes.

tour.title: Static Chat SPA
tour.description: GET / returns frontend/index.html, the shell for chat, the sidebar, upload, and citations. It links the stylesheets and loads the browser scripts, ending with app.js. app.js keeps session and mode state and runs the send pipeline: persist the user message, retrieve RAG chunks, optionally search the web, then stream a Puter.js completion. api.js is the window.API client for those FastAPI calls, config.example.js shows the BACKEND_URL and Puter token placeholder that client reads, and puter_client.js builds mode-specific system prompts that inject the RAG excerpts and search results.
tour.languageLesson: These are classic global scripts, not ES modules. Each file attaches an object to window, and index.html loads them in dependency order so later files can call earlier ones.

tour.title: Transcript and Theme
tour.description: Once the send pipeline has a reply, these files decide how the turn looks. chat.js builds user and assistant bubbles, streams tokens with thought steps and citation cards, and restores prior session history. It uses utils.js for markdown, citation badges, syntax highlighting, and timestamps, and ui.js for the citation modal, session and document lists, toasts, and the file drop overlay. main.css defines the dark-by-default tokens and the app shell; components.css styles messages, citations, and the input dock with those tokens.
tour.languageLesson: CSS custom properties on the root selector act as design tokens. Component rules reference those variables, and a light-theme override reassigns the same names so the layout stays in one place.

tour.title: Streamlit and API Client
tour.description: frontend/app.py is the Streamlit UI for the same backend. It keeps session state, renders chat and document controls, and calls FastAPI at BACKEND_URL (default http://localhost:8000) for chat, history, PDF upload, and document listing. backend/client.py is the Python HTTP client that covers the routes you already traced: health, models, sessions, upload, retrieval, and web search. The Streamlit page is a full UI; the client class is how another Python process can call the same API.

tour.title: Container and Deploy
tour.description: With the request path clear, these two files show how the processes start. .devcontainer/devcontainer.json uses a Python 3.11 image, installs project requirements and Streamlit, forwards FastAPI on port 8000 and Streamlit on 8501, and starts frontend/app.py when the container attaches. The Procfile starts the FastAPI app with uvicorn and binds to the platform-assigned port for Render or Railway. One file reproduces the local loop; the other is the hosted command for the API entry point.
tour.languageLesson: A Dev Container spec pins the image, the install step, and the forwarded ports so every machine boots the same toolchain. A Procfile process type is one command the platform runs, and binding to the assigned PORT lets the host route traffic to uvicorn.
